MS.AAD.2.1v1.t: Users detected as high risk SHALL be blocked.

MS.AAD.2.2v1.t: A notification SHOULD be sent to the administrator when high-risk users are detected.

MS.AAD.2.3v1.t: Sign-ins detected as high-risk SHALL be blocked.

MS.AAD.3.1v1.t: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.

MS.AAD.3.2v2.t: MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.

MS.AAD.3.3v2.t: If Microsoft Authenticator is enabled, it SHALL be configured to show login context information.

MS.AAD.3.4v1.t: The "Authentication methods manage migration" feature SHALL be set to "Migration complete."

MS.AAD.3.5v2.t: The authentication methods of short message service (SMS), voice call, and email one-time passcode (OTP) SHALL be disabled.

MS.AAD.3.6v1.t: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be required for highly privileged roles.

MS.AAD.3.7v1.t: Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.

MS.AAD.3.8v1.t: Managed devices SHOULD be required to register MFA.

MS.AAD.3.9v1.t: Device code authentication SHOULD be blocked.

MS.AAD.4.1v1.t: Security logs SHALL be sent to the agency's security operations center for monitoring.

MS.AAD.5.1v1.t: Only administrators SHALL be allowed to register applications.

MS.AAD.5.2v1.t: User consent to applications SHALL be restricted.

MS.AAD.5.3v1.t: An administrative consent workflow SHALL be configured for applications.

MS.AAD.5.5v1.t: Application password addition SHOULD be blocked.

MS.AAD.5.6v1.t: Application password lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 180 days or less.

MS.AAD.5.7v1.t: Application certificate lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 365 days or less.

MS.AAD.7.1v1.t: A minimum of two users and a maximum of eight users SHALL be provisioned with the Global Administrator role.

MS.AAD.7.2v1.t: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned with finer-grained roles instead of the Global Administrator role.

MS.AAD.7.3v1.t: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned cloud-only accounts separate from an on-premises directory or other federated identity providers.

MS.AAD.7.4v1.t: Permanent active role assignments SHALL NOT be allowed for highly privileged roles.

MS.AAD.7.5v1.t: Provisioning users to highly privileged roles SHALL NOT occur outside of a PAM system.

MS.AAD.7.6v1.t: Activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL require approval.

MS.AAD.7.7v1.t: Eligible and active highly privileged role assignments SHALL trigger an alert.

MS.AAD.7.8v1.t: User activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL trigger an alert.

MS.AAD.7.9v1.t: User activation of other highly privileged roles SHOULD trigger an alert.

MS.AAD.8.1v1.t: Guest users SHOULD have limited or restricted access to Microsoft Entra ID directory objects.

MS.AAD.8.2v1.t: Only users with the "Guest Inviter" role SHOULD be able to invite guest users.

MS.AAD.8.3v1.t: Guest invites SHOULD only be allowed to be sent to specific external domains that have been authorized by the agency for legitimate business purposes.

MS.AAD.9.1v1.t: Risky AI agents SHALL be blocked.

MS.EXO.1.1v2.t: Automatic forwarding to external domains SHALL be disabled.

MS.EXO.2.2v3.t: An SPF policy SHALL be published for each domain that fails all non-approved senders.

MS.EXO.3.1v1.t: DKIM SHOULD be enabled for all domains.

MS.EXO.4.1v1.t: A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.

MS.EXO.4.2v1.t: The DMARC message rejection option SHALL be p=reject.

MS.EXO.4.3v1.t: The DMARC point of contact for aggregate reports SHALL include reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov.

MS.EXO.4.4v1.t: An agency point of contact SHOULD be included for aggregate and failure reports.

MS.EXO.6.1v1.t: Contact folders SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.

MS.EXO.6.2v1.t: Calendar details SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.

MS.EXO.7.1v1.t: External sender warnings SHALL be implemented.

MS.POWERBI.1.1v1.t: The "Publish to Web" feature SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.

MS.POWERBI.2.1v1.t: Guest user access to the Power BI tenant SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.

MS.POWERBI.3.1v1.t: The "Invite external users to your organization" feature SHOULD be disabled unless agency mission requires the capability.

MS.POWERBI.4.1v1.t: Service principals with access to APIs SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.

MS.POWERBI.4.2v1.t: Service principals' ability to create and use profiles SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.

MS.POWERBI.5.1v1.t: ResourceKey-based authentication SHOULD be blocked unless a specific use case (e.g., streaming and/or "push" datasets) merits its use.

MS.POWERBI.6.1v1.t: Python and R interactions SHOULD be disabled.

MS.POWERBI.7.1v1.t: Sensitivity labels SHOULD be enabled for Power BI and employed for sensitive data per enterprise data protection policies.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.1.1v1.t: The ability to create production and sandbox environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.1.2v1.t: The ability to create trial environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.1v1.t: A DLP policy SHALL be created to restrict connector access in the default Power Platform environment.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.2v1.t: Non-default environments SHOULD have at least one DLP policy.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.3.1v1.t: Power Platform tenant isolation SHALL be enabled.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.3.2v1.t: An inbound/outbound connection allowlist SHOULD be configured.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.4.1v1.t: Content Security Policy (CSP) SHALL be enforced for model-driven and canvas Power Apps.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.5.1v1.t: The ability to create Power Pages sites SHOULD be restricted to administrators.

MS.POWERPLATFORM.6.1v1.t: The "Share with everyone" feature SHOULD be disabled.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.1v1.t: Emails with click-to-run file attachments SHALL be blocked including, at a minimum, .exe, .cmd, and .vbe files.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.2v1.t: Email scanning SHALL be capable of reviewing emails after delivery.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.3v1.t: Emails identified as containing malware SHALL be quarantined or dropped.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.4v1.t: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams message attachments SHOULD be scanned for malware.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.1v1.t: User impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for sensitive accounts.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.2v1.t: Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for domains owned by the agency.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.3v1.t: Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be added for key suppliers and partners.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.4v1.t: User warnings, comparable to the user safety tips included with EOP, SHOULD be displayed.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.1v1.t: A DLP policy SHALL be configured to protect PII and sensitive information, as defined by the agency, blocking at a minimum: credit card numbers, U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN), and U.S. Social Security numbers (SSN).

MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.2v1.t: The DLP policy SHOULD be applied to Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams chat, and Devices.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.3v1.t: The action for the DLP policy SHOULD be set to block sharing sensitive information with everyone.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.4v1.t: Notifications to inform users and help educate them on the proper use of sensitive information SHOULD be enabled in the DLP policy.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.5v1.t: The DLP policy SHOULD include an action to block access to sensitive information by restricted applications and unwanted Bluetooth applications.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.4.1v1.t: At a minimum, the following alerts SHALL be enabled:

MS.SECURITYSUITE.4.2v1.t: The alerts SHOULD be sent to a monitored address or incorporated into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).

MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.1v1.t: Unified audit logging SHALL be enabled.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.2v1.t: Audit logs SHALL be retained and searchable for a minimum of 3 months and retrievable for a minimum of 12 months.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.1v1.t: Emails detected as spam and phishing SHALL NOT be delivered to the user's inbox.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.2v1.t: Allowed domains SHALL NOT be added to inbound anti-spam protection policies.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.1v1.t: URL comparison with a block-list SHOULD be enabled for URLs in emails, Teams messages, and Office documents.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.2v1.t: Direct download links SHOULD be scanned for malware.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.3v1.t: User click tracking SHOULD be enabled.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.8.1v1.t: IP allow lists SHOULD NOT be created.

MS.SECURITYSUITE.8.2v1.t: Safe lists SHOULD NOT be enabled.

MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1v1.t: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."

MS.SHAREPOINT.1.2v1.t: External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."

MS.SHAREPOINT.1.3v1.t: External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.

MS.SHAREPOINT.2.1v1.t: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)."

MS.SHAREPOINT.2.2v1.t: File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to view only.

MS.SHAREPOINT.3.1v1.t: Expiration days for "Anyone" links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2v1.t: The allowable file and folder permissions for links SHALL be set to view only.

MS.SHAREPOINT.3.3v2.t: Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

MS.TEAMS.1.1v1.t: External meeting participants SHOULD NOT be enabled to request control of shared desktops or windows.

MS.TEAMS.1.2v2.t: Anonymous users SHALL NOT be enabled to start Microsoft Teams meetings.

MS.TEAMS.1.3v1.t: Anonymous users and dial-in callers SHOULD NOT be admitted automatically.

MS.TEAMS.1.4v1.t: Internal users SHOULD be admitted to Microsoft Teams meetings automatically.

MS.TEAMS.1.5v1.t: Dial-in users SHOULD NOT be enabled to bypass the lobby.

MS.TEAMS.1.7v2.t: "Record an event" SHOULD NOT be set to "Always record."

MS.TEAMS.2.1v2.t: External access for users SHALL only be enabled on a per-domain basis.

MS.TEAMS.2.2v2.t: Unmanaged users SHALL NOT be enabled to initiate contact with internal users.

MS.TEAMS.2.3v2.t: Internal users SHOULD NOT be enabled to initiate contact with unmanaged users.

MS.TEAMS.4.1v1.t: Microsoft Teams email integration SHALL be disabled.

MS.TEAMS.5.1v2.t: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of Microsoft applications approved by the agency.

MS.TEAMS.5.2v2.t: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of third-party applications approved by the agency.

MS.TEAMS.5.3v2.t: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of custom applications approved by the agency.
